new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The target lists only one work and the reader opened and read it, so there was no listed silent-or-unopened work to spot-check beyond re-reading this one in full. As a further spot-check I re-a full-text search for stress/accent the three files our earlier reading had saved in the same folder (Shimizu 1996 Kulu vocabulary, utf8 text; Blench 2006 Kulu wordlist text; Watters 2017 ch. 4 text): stress 0 / accent 0 in all three; the 'prominent' hits are unrelated (Shimizu line 271 'Some prominent rules of phonological changes'; Watters lines 1026, 2079, 2261 about noun-class features). sources.note: Nothing. Part One §1 Phonology covers vowels (1.1), consonants (1.2), tones (1.3: 'There are three distinct tone levels..'; composite/falling tones; tone-bearing sonorants), phonological changes (1.4), intonation (1.5). Preface §4: 'It has three distinct level tones, which are sometimes contracted to falling tones.' No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole document.

sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Ikulu beyond Shimizu's web notes (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch, 72 pp, German); a Hamburg Afrikanistik thesis under Gerhardt would normally include a Phonologie chapter with a Ton/Akzent subsection — the one place a stress/accent statement for Ikulu could exist. Glottolog/MPI-EVA hold a scan.
